title: Classical module sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring. The full
subcategory of classical sheaves in $\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda_X)$ contains $0$
and is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions: if $f\colon G\to G'$ is a
map of classical module sheaves, then $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{coker}f$ are
classical, and if $0\to G'\to E\to G\to0$ is exact with $G,G'$ classical, then
$E$ is classical.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-encoding] to identify intrinsic constant-ring modules with ModuleCat-valued sheaves. Restriction retains their underlying additive sheaves, and its inverse does so up to the equivalence counit. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], classicality is therefore the essential image of the composite T of the exact fully faithful comparison inverse image L and this encoding equivalence. T preserves zero, kernels and cokernels.

For a map $f:G	o G'$ with $G\cong
u_X^*F$ and $G'\cong
u_X^*F'$, full faithfulness gives a unique $\varphi:F	o F'$ with $f\cong
u_X^*\varphi$. Exactness of $
u_X^*$ identifies $\ker(f)$ with $
u_X^*\ker(\varphi)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(f)$ with $
u_X^*\operatorname{coker}(\varphi)$; both are classical by the essential-image clause of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules].

Use the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] with ModuleCat in universe u+1. The module category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], and its pro-etale sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck]. Thus [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] gives enough injectives. The comparison adjunction R is additive and left exact, as restriction on sections in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; its exact fully faithful left adjoint L is [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. The extension argument can be made in ModuleCat-valued sheaves and transported back by the encoding equivalence.

Let $0\to G\xrightarrow{a}E\xrightarrow{b}H\to0$ be exact with $G\cong LF$ and $H\cong LF_1$ classical. Apply [sk-prop-sf-comparison] to the degree-zero complex $F[0]\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$: its derived unit is an isomorphism $F[0]\cong R\nu_{X,*}(LF[0])$. The single-object identification [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], with the abelian categories and enough injectives supplied in step 3, identifies its degree-one cohomology with $R^1\nu_{X,*}(LF)$.

Apply the cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in degree $1$ to the isomorphism in step 4. It preserves isomorphisms, so $R^1\nu_{X,*}(LF)\cong H^1(F[0])$. In the complex $F[0]$, the terms in degrees $1$ and $2$ are zero, hence $\ker(d^1)=0$ and $\operatorname{im}(d^0)=0$; thus $H^1(F[0])=0/0=0$. The isomorphism $G\cong LF$ therefore gives $R^1\nu_{X,*}G=0$.

The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] applies to the left exact additive $R=\nu_{X,*}$ and the sequence in step 4, by step 3. Using the natural identification $R^0R\cong R$ of [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], its beginning is $0\to RG\xrightarrow{Ra}RE\xrightarrow{Rb}RH\to R^1RG$. Step 5 makes the last term zero. Exactness consequently says $Rb$ is an epimorphism, giving a short exact sequence $0\to RG\to RE\to RH\to0$.

Apply the exact $L$ of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] to the short exact sequence in step 6. Together with the sequence in step 4, the counits form two short exact rows with vertical maps $\varepsilon_G:LRG\to G$, $\varepsilon_E:LRE\to E$ and $\varepsilon_H:LRH\to H$. The squares commute by the equations $a\varepsilon_G=\varepsilon_E LR(a)$ and $b\varepsilon_E=\varepsilon_H LR(b)$ expressing naturality of the counit. Since $L$ is fully faithful, the adjunction identifies its Hom bijection with postcomposition by $\eta_F:F\to RLF$. Taking the source to be $RLF$ yields $t:RLF\to F$ with $\eta_F t=1$; injectivity for source $F$ then gives $t\eta_F=1$, since $\eta_F(t\eta_F)=\eta_F$. Thus $\eta_F$ is invertible. The triangle identity $\varepsilon_{LF}\,L\eta_F=1_{LF}$ now makes $\varepsilon_{LF}$ invertible; naturality with the isomorphisms $G\cong LF$ and $H\cong LF_1$ makes $\varepsilon_G$ and $\varepsilon_H$ invertible. The short five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] makes $\varepsilon_E$ invertible. Hence $E\cong LRE$ lies in the classical essential image of $L$, as required.
